Definition: An internist is a personal physician who provides long-term, comprehensive care in the office and the hospital, managing both common and complex illness of adolescents, adults and the elderly.
A cardiologist specializes in diseases of the heart, lungs and blood vessels and manages complex cardiac conditions such as heart attacks and life-threatening, abnormal heartbeat rhythms.
An internist who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of all types of cancer and other benign and malignant tumors.
An internist with additional training who specializes in hematology (disorders of blood, bone marrow, and lymph glands) and medical oncology.
A physician who provides care based on knowledge of the patient in the context of the family and the community, emphasizing disease prevention and health promotion.
A psychiatrist specializes in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of mental illness. The psychiatrist is qualified to assess both the mental and physical aspects of psychological disturbance.

Grouping: Physician Assistants & Advanced Practice Nursing Providers
Definition: (1) A registered nurse provider of health care services who has specialized education and training. (2) An individual who has graduated from a formal advanced nursing education program.

Grouping: Physician Assistants & Advanced Practice Nursing Providers
Definition: A nurse practitioner who has completed an advanced practice program to serve as a primary care provider for adults.
An individual who is licensed to prepare and dispense drugs pursuant to a prescription.
A pharmacy where pharmacists store, prepare, and dispense medicinal preparations and/or prescriptions for a local patient population.
A pharmacy maintained in a hospital that is authorized to compound, dispense, and supply drugs and medicines to patients of the hospital.
A podiatrist is a person qualified by a Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (D.P.M.) degree, licensed by the state, and practicing within the scope of that license.
A supplier of medical equipment such as respirators, wheelchairs and other medically necessary equipment and supplies.
A clinic located in a rural medically underserved area in the United States that has a separate reimbursement structure from the standard medical office.
An institution whose primary function is to provide inpatient diagnostic and therapeutic services for a variety of medical conditions, both surgical and non-surgical.
A physical therapist provides services that help restore function, improve mobility, relieve pain, and prevent or limit permanent physical disabilities in patients.

Grouping: Physician Assistants & Advanced Practice Nursing Providers
Definition: A registered nurse who has completed a full course in an accredited nurse anesthesia educational program and is competent in the practice of anesthesia.
A specialist provides services in a specific field of medicine.
A health care practitioner who specializes in the manual adjustment or manipulation of the spinal column.
A person trained and certified to plan, prepare, and serve food in institutions.
